name: Augustus
line: The first emperor: found Rome brick and left it marble, and left the Republic in name only.
exitNote: Died at Nola on 19 August AD 14, aged 75. "Have I played the part well? Then applaud as I exit."

name: Tiberius
line: Capable, gloomy, and eventually absent: he ran the last decade of his reign from Capri.
exitNote: Died at Misenum on 16 March 37, aged 77. Rumours of a helpful pillow were never proven.

name: Caligula
line: Began popular, ended as the byword for tyranny. The horse-as-consul story is probably a joke he made about the Senate.
exitNote: Stabbed by Praetorian officers led by Cassius Chaerea, 24 January 41.

name: Claudius
line: The underestimated scholar who conquered Britain, built the port at Ostia, and married badly.
exitNote: Died 13 October 54, reportedly after a dish of mushrooms arranged by Agrippina.

name: Nero
line: Artist, matricide, builder of the Golden House; the last of the Julio-Claudians.
exitNote: Declared a public enemy by the Senate; stabbed himself, with assistance, on 9 June 68. "Qualis artifex pereo."

name: Vespasian
line: Restored order after the Year of the Four Emperors, began the Colosseum, and taxed urine.
exitNote: Died 23 June 79. Allegedly: "Vae, puto deus fio" — "Dear me, I think I'm becoming a god."

name: Titus
line: Took Jerusalem in 70, opened the Colosseum in 80, handled Vesuvius and a fire; died young and beloved.
exitNote: Died 13 September 81 after just over two years. Domitian succeeded.

name: Domitian
line: An efficient autocrat loathed by the Senate, who rebuilt Rome and stabilised the coinage.
exitNote: Stabbed by court officials on 18 September 96. The Senate voted to erase his memory.

name: Nerva
line: The elderly senator who started the run of "Five Good Emperors" by adopting Trajan.
exitNote: Died 27 January 98 after sixteen months in office.

name: Trajan
line: Optimus princeps: conquered Dacia, built the Forum and the Column, and took the Empire to its greatest extent.
exitNote: Died at Selinus in Cilicia in August 117, on his way home from Parthia.

name: Hadrian
line: Consolidator, traveller, builder of the Wall and the Pantheon. Wore a beard; the Senate never forgave him.
exitNote: Died at Baiae on 10 July 138 after a long illness. "Animula vagula blandula…"

name: Antoninus Pius
line: Twenty-three years of peace, a budget surplus, and almost no travel. The Empire's quietest reign.
exitNote: Died at Lorium on 7 March 161. His last watchword to the guard: "aequanimitas".

name: Marcus Aurelius
line: The Stoic philosopher who spent his reign on the Danube fighting the Marcomanni and writing the Meditations.
exitNote: Died near Sirmium or at Vindobona on 17 March 180. Then Commodus happened.

name: Commodus
line: The gladiator-emperor who renamed Rome after himself. Gladiator (2000) got the vibe, not the facts.
exitNote: Strangled in his bath by the wrestler Narcissus on 31 December 192.

name: Pertinax
line: A reforming emperor for 86 days.
exitNote: Killed by the Praetorians on 28 March 193, who then auctioned the Empire to Didius Julianus.

name: Septimius Severus
line: The African-born soldier-emperor. "Enrich the soldiers and scorn everyone else."
exitNote: Died at Eboracum (York) on 4 February 211, on campaign in Britain.

name: Caracalla
line: Murdered his brother Geta, granted citizenship to the whole Empire (212), built the Baths.
exitNote: Stabbed while relieving himself by the roadside near Carrhae on 8 April 217, on Macrinus's orders.

name: Elagabalus
line: The teenage priest of a Syrian sun god whose reign scandalised Rome — the sources are hostile and vivid.
exitNote: Killed by the Praetorians with his mother on 11 March 222; body thrown into the Tiber.

name: Severus Alexander
line: The last Severan; a mild ruler whose murder opened the Crisis of the Third Century.
exitNote: Killed by mutinous troops near Moguntiacum (Mainz) in March 235.

name: Maximinus Thrax
line: The first soldier-emperor from the ranks; never set foot in Rome.
exitNote: Killed by his own troops while besieging Aquileia in 238.

name: Decius
line: Persecutor of Christians and the first emperor to die in battle against a foreign enemy.
exitNote: Fell at Abritus against the Goths in June 251, with his son.

name: Valerian
line: The only emperor ever taken prisoner by a foreign power.
exitNote: Captured by Shapur I near Edessa in 260; reportedly used as a footstool. Died a Persian prisoner.

name: Gallienus
line: Held the centre while Gaul and Palmyra broke away; reformed the cavalry.
exitNote: Killed by his own officers outside Milan in 268.

name: Aurelian
line: Restitutor Orbis: beat Palmyra and the Gallic Empire, walled Rome, and reunified the Empire in five years.
exitNote: Murdered by his officers near Byzantium in late 275, after a forged execution list.

name: Diocletian
line: Reorganised everything — tetrarchy, provinces, taxes, prices — then retired to grow cabbages at Split.
exitNote: Abdicated 1 May 305; died c. 311/312 in his palace at Spalatum. The only emperor to retire voluntarily.

name: Constantine the Great
line: Won at the Milvian Bridge, legalised Christianity, founded Constantinople, reunified the Empire.
exitNote: Died near Nicomedia on 22 May 337, baptised on his deathbed.

name: Julian
line: "The Apostate": the philosopher-soldier who tried to restore the old gods.
exitNote: Mortally wounded in Persia on 26 June 363. "Vicisti, Galilaee" is probably an invention.

name: Valens
line: The Eastern emperor who let the Goths across the Danube, then fought them.
exitNote: Died at Adrianople on 9 August 378; his body was never found.

name: Theodosius I
line: The last emperor to rule both halves; made Nicene Christianity the state religion.
exitNote: Died at Milan on 17 January 395; the Empire was divided between his sons Arcadius and Honorius.

name: Honorius
line: Presided, from Ravenna, over the sack of Rome in 410 — reportedly more worried about his chicken, also named Roma.
exitNote: Died in Ravenna on 15 August 423.

name: Majorian
line: The last Western emperor who seriously tried to restore the state — Gibbon's "great and heroic character".
exitNote: Deposed and beheaded by his general Ricimer on 7 August 461.

name: Romulus Augustulus
line: Teenage figurehead and last Western emperor; "Augustulus" means "little Augustus".
exitNote: Deposed by Odoacer on 4 September 476 and pensioned off to Campania. Fate unknown. This site counts from his last day.

name: Zeno
line: Received the Western regalia from Odoacer in 476. From Constantinople, the "end of the Western Empire" looked like an administrative tidy-up.
exitNote: Died on 9 April 491. A later legend says he was buried alive. Probably not.

name: Justinian I
line: Reconquered Africa and Italy, codified Roman law, built Hagia Sophia: "the emperor who never sleeps".
exitNote: Died 14 November 565, aged about 83.

name: Heraclius
line: Defeated Persia, lost Syria and Egypt to the Arabs; made Greek official and took the title Basileus.
exitNote: Died 11 February 641.

name: Leo III the Isaurian
line: Broke the Arab siege of 717–718 and started Iconoclasm.
exitNote: Died 18 June 741 of dropsy.

name: Basil II
line: "The Bulgar-slayer": the Empire's medieval peak, with a full treasury.
exitNote: Died 15 December 1025 while planning an invasion of Sicily — unmarried, childless, and unbeaten.

name: Alexios I Komnenos
line: Stabilised the Empire after Manzikert and asked the West for mercenaries. Got the First Crusade instead.
exitNote: Died 15 August 1118.

name: Constantine XI Palaiologos
line: The last Roman emperor; died defending the Theodosian Walls.
exitNote: Fell on 29 May 1453; body never conclusively identified. The "Marble Emperor" legend says he sleeps until the city is retaken. We check daily.
